mission: Investigate effective versus advertised language-model context capacity using nine verified, accessible primary research sources. Examine how retrieval position, context length, lexical overlap, distractor complexity, information aggregation, multi-hop reasoning, realistic document structure, and citation accuracy affect performance. Distinguish a model's ability to accept long inputs from its demonstrated ability to locate, integrate, reason over, and faithfully cite information within those inputs. Investigate positional effects through Lost in the Middle; synthetic retrieval, aggregation and multi-hop behavior through RULER; semantic retrieval without literal matching through NoLiMa; realistic multi-document and repository reasoning through LongBench and LongBench v2; distributed-fact reasoning through BABILong; application-specific evaluation validity through HELMET; contexts exceeding 100K tokens through InfinityBench; and evidence attribution through LongCite. Capture exact model identities, evaluation dates, dataset construction, task definitions, context lengths, quantitative outcomes, uncertainty, and stated limitations before candidate construction. Distinguish historical benchmark findings from present model capabilities. Do not treat benchmark scores from different datasets as directly comparable, simple needle retrieval as proof of full-context understanding, correct answers as proof of citation faithfulness, or advertised context windows as verified effective context lengths. Preserve the distinction between experiments, interpretations, and proposed explanations. Do not infer independent replication from overlapping benchmark datasets or evaluation suites. Prioritize distinct, narrowly scoped, source-grounded assertions over record count. All source requests are for subsequent immutable compiler capture and independent entailment and adversarial review. Do not modify broad existing field or frontier-question records, invent scientific relationships or taxonomy placement, or assert current frontier status.
